intents: Configure logical tenant separation on r1 using Linux VRF devices.
tenant-blue is connected to r1 eth1 on 10.10.1.0/24.
tenant-red is connected to r1 eth2 on 10.20.1.0/24.
shared is dual-attached: eth1 is the blue shared segment 10.10.100.0/24 and eth2 is the red shared segment 10.20.100.0/24.
Create VRF vrf-blue with table 10 and VRF vrf-red with table 20.
Place r1 eth1 and eth3 in vrf-blue, and r1 eth2 and eth4 in vrf-red.
Assign gateway addresses on r1 and enable IPv4 forwarding.
Allow each tenant to reach only its shared service segment, while tenant-blue and tenant-red remain isolated from each other.
Do not modify management connectivity on eth0.

r1: ip link add vrf-blue type vrf table 10
ip link add vrf-red type vrf table 20
ip link set eth1 master vrf-blue
ip link set eth3 master vrf-blue
ip link set eth2 master vrf-red
ip link set eth4 master vrf-red

ground_truth_reasoning: The tenant-facing and shared-facing interfaces are separated into two Linux VRF devices so each tenant has an independent routing table. vrf-blue contains tenant-blue and the blue shared segment; vrf-red contains tenant-red and the red shared segment. This provides a controlled service leak through the dual-attached shared node while avoiding any route between the tenant-blue and tenant-red LANs. Enabling IPv4 forwarding lets r1 route within each VRF only.

baseline_invariants.name: tenant-blue management interface is still up
r1 management interface is still up
tenant-red management interface is still up
shared management interface is still up
r1 management default route is preserved
Strict safety: tenant-blue cannot reach tenant-red
Strict safety: tenant-red cannot reach tenant-blue
